newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Megawati lawyer attacks trials of supporters.
newsitem.headline: Megawati lawyer attacks trials of supporters.

text.p: The trials of 124 supporters of ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri were designed to put political pressure on the embattled politician, her chief defence lawyer said on Tuesday.

R.O. Tambunan, his voice sometimes cracking with emotion, told a packed session at the Central Jakarta State Court that the defendants were being tried not for any criminal act but because they were Megawati supporters.
The 124 accused have been charged with assault and disobeying police orders to disperse on July 27 after a police raid on the Jakarta offices of Megawati's Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
The accused had occupied the headquarters in protest against the ousting of Megawati as PDI leader by a rival party faction.
The riots that followed saw some of the worst violence in Jakarta in more than 20 years.

"The case of the 124 PDI members who are Megawati supporters now being tried is a case which has political aims," Tambunan told the trial, sometimes wiping tears from his eyes, as Megawati and her senior party supporters watched behind him in court.

"The powerholders aim to put pressure on Megawati and her friends, to paralyse her political influence and strength as well as use it for bargaining so Megawati will acknowledge the results of the Medan congress," he said.
"The 124 accused have been brought before the court not because they have done any criminal action but because they are followers and supporters of Megawati," Tambunan said.

The defence called on the panel of three judges to release the accused and the dismiss all the charges. Chief Judge Sjoffinan Sumantri adjourned the case and said a decision would be announced on November 27.
Megawati, who sat silently fanning herself through the four-hour session in the stifling courtroom, said after the case that she would wait for the verdict.

"It is important to listen to the opinion of the people," she later told reporters when asked to comment on the proceedings. About 100 supporters gathered in and outside the court and security around the complex was lighter than usual with no incidents reported.

Megawati, the daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted by the deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi in June at a special party congress in Medan, North Sumatra which was financed by the government and backed by the armed forces.
She called the result illegal and challenged it in a case which has been appealed to the Jakarta High Court after a lower court ruled in September it did not have the authority to rule on the case.
The defence statement attacked the police handling of the case as none of the more than 200 Surjadi red-shirted supporters who attacked the PDI headquarters on July 27 have been arrested.
